title: Relay briefs pin a resumed headless role to the slice worktree and repeat the no-cd rule
lead: `slicer ai relay` and `slicer ai relay-orchestrator` say in Every brief that every role, the read-only ones included, uses absolute paths and `git -C` and never `cd`, and the orchestrator text says that a resumed headless role is given the slice worktree as its working directory and that the orchestrator checks the directory the role reports before it goes on.
findings_note: s384 relay report 2026-10-22, later notes 4 and 5: a reviewer used `cd` twice in read-only commands, and a resumed Codex implementer started in the main checkout, not the worktree (main was left clean)
boundary: **Not in this slice:** the role matrix, a hook or harness setting that blocks `cd`, any change to how `relay-run` records steps, and the contract bump (s424 bumps to v11 once for all of v1.17).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
The relay brief's environment lines already say "No `cd`: absolute paths and `git -C`", yet a read-only reviewer ran `cd` twice, which the owner's rules forbid. The relay text keeps the git-write ban in the contract (`src/slicer/ai.py`, the "Every brief" section) but not the no-`cd` rule, so a reviewer, architect or gate brief can omit it. Separately, `slicer ai relay-orchestrator` says to resume the role that raised the blockers but not that a headless role, resumed, must be given the slice worktree as its working directory. A Codex implementer resumed in the main checkout could write there. The orchestrator found `main` clean, so nothing was damaged this time.

Owner decision 2026-10-30: every v1.17 rule change lands at v10 text and s424 bumps to v11 once, last. This slice does not touch `RELAY_CONTRACT` or `RELAY_CHANGES`.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/ai.py`: `RELAY_BRIEF` (the "Every brief" paragraph, beside "Reviewer, architect and gate briefs forbid git writes") and `ORCHESTRATOR_RULES` (the Gate resume rule and the Waiting rule's "resume it and tell it to finish").
- `tests/test_ai.py`, next to `test_AiRelayOrchestrator_Text_NamesParentDisputesGateResume`; `tests/fixtures/relay-contract-v10.json` regenerated for the new text.
- `docs/agents.md` or `docs/working-with-agents.md` only where it quotes that text; `CHANGELOG.md` under Changed.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `test_AiRelay_EveryBrief_ForbidsCdForEachRole`: the relay text says every role, the read-only ones included, uses absolute paths and `git -C`, never `cd`.
- `test_AiRelayOrchestrator_Resume_PinsHeadlessWorkdir`: the orchestrator text says that resuming a headless role names the slice worktree as its working directory and that the orchestrator checks the role's reported directory before it works.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the tests; watch them go red.
2. Add the no-`cd` sentence beside the git-write ban, and the resume-workdir rule to the orchestrator's Gate/Waiting rules. Keep Gate, Every brief, Stop and Conformance identical across both texts (`relay_shared_sections`).
3. Regenerate the golden; update the docs and CHANGELOG. Leave `RELAY_CONTRACT` at 10; record the rule change in the closing note for s424's `RELAY_CHANGES` entry.
4. Mutation-check each new test.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: - `python3 tests/affected.py --run`, then the full suite. `slicer check` passes.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch; the owner lands it.
